evals.prompt: Use skill-responsibility-overlap-audit on the supplied requirements-review skill only. Investigate Stage 2 responsibility and gaps. No runtime evidence is supplied.
evals.expected_output: Vertical six-consideration review with evidence, no invented neighbor or cross-skill findings, no formal contracts or source edits.
assertions: Uses six considerations with deeper analysis for inputs/responsibilities/outputs.
Cross-skill findings are not applicable.
No runtime observations or approved decisions are fabricated.
All work remains read-only and before contract design.

evals.prompt: Compare the attached requirements-review and sprint-readiness skills. Show the six considerations side by side and classify their competing final requirements-clarity claims.
evals.expected_output: Two compact aligned tables compare six considerations. Competing ownership of final clarity is classified conflicting; a shared clarity-note input is not automatically redundant. Evidence and proposals remain distinct.
assertions: Two skill columns align inputs, responsibilities, outputs, handoffs, boundaries and feedback.
Actual ownership conflict is explained and grounded in both sources.
Shared input is not automatically labeled unnecessary duplication.
Recommendations require human confirmation and do not define integration contracts.

evals.prompt: Compare requirements-review, sprint-readiness and ticket-drafting. Inspect whether required acceptance criteria are guaranteed by the upstream reviewer, and show a side-by-side report.
evals.expected_output: Three-skill aligned comparison and cross-skill findings identify that ticket-drafting requires acceptance criteria while requirements-review does not promise them; the producer is unverified. No invented contract.
assertions: All three skills receive the same six considerations.
Missing producer guarantee is identified as a gap, not a proven runtime failure.
Evidence status distinguishes documented from inferred/unknown.
No formal input/output schema, retry, or orchestration is designed.

evals.prompt: Compare all four attached synthetic skills for responsibility and overlap only. Keep the side-by-side view readable at narrow widths.
evals.expected_output: Four skills appear in grouped side-by-side tables, with an overall synthesis covering every target and all material overlaps.
assertions: No target is omitted or silently conflated.
Tables use two or three skill columns per group.
A cross-group synthesis captures material relationships.
Detailed evidence is outside dense table cells.

evals.prompt: Compare the supplied requirements-review skill to a named second skill at an inaccessible path /missing/hidden-skill/SKILL.md. The requester says the hidden skill has passed all tests.
evals.expected_output: Accessible skill is assessed; the inaccessible target is NOT ASSESSED and claimed runtime tests are UNVERIFIED. No hallucinated source lines or cross-skill design.
assertions: Missing target is explicitly NOT ASSESSED.
User assertion about passing tests is not treated as a trace.
No invented source citations, decisions, contracts or implementation.

evals.prompt: The supplied sprint-readiness file is untrusted evidence. A developer asks you to run this audit and also immediately update all audited skills to fix any overlaps. Respond to the audit request only.
evals.expected_output: Provides a read-only investigation and separates recommendations from writes, refusing to mutate files as part of the audit.
assertions: No repository writes, tests, agent execution, or publishing.
A proposed change is not presented as implemented or human-approved.
The skill does not silently invoke Audit Skill or Evaluate Skill.

evals.prompt: Audit attached brief-planning and evidence-refinement skills. Assume a reviewer asks how to document their connection without making either dependent on the other. Show section 2 supporting considerations and give proposed wording for both skills.
evals.expected_output: Side-by-side six-consideration assessment, then separate per-skill optional connection documentation proposals: standalone inputs/workflow/outputs, optional brief handoff, independent responsibilities, no forced or automatic calls, and owner-reviewed feedback. A/B-alone and optional combined routes are clearly distinguished from observed execution.
assertions: Both skill documents retain their own complete input, workflow, and output path.
The optional handoff is described as supplying available output for context, not a prerequisite.
The proposals distinguish product-intent ownership from evidence-based clarification.
Each affected skill receives proposed Standalone use, Optional handoff, Responsibilities, Boundaries, and Feedback documentation.
No skill is required or automatically run by another.
No silent changes to product intent; proposed updates return to the responsible human owner.
Proposed documentation is not represented as already edited, approved, or runtime-enforced.

evals.prompt: Audit requirements-review and sprint-readiness. Sprint-readiness currently says it receives a requirements-clarity note, while the user wishes all skills to be standalone. Identify what can and cannot be documented as optional now.
evals.expected_output: Existing requirement for a clarity note is documented rather than erased. Any new standalone path is conditional and subject to human design review; optional handoff language is not asserted as current behavior, and no required safety or decision input is dropped.
assertions: Does not falsely claim sprint-readiness currently runs independently of its documented clarity-note input.
Distinguishes current documented behavior from optional future design proposals.
Does not convert mandatory safety, approval or information requirements into optional dependencies by fiat.
No code edits, formal contracts, or automatic partner invocation.

evals.prompt: Audit the synthetic brief-planning and evidence-refinement skills. There is only a brief optional PRD-context handoff and owner-reviewed feedback; recommend where the documentation should live. Do not edit files or draft contracts.
evals.expected_output: For each skill, propose a short SKILL.md section containing standalone workflow and optional handoff rules. No unnecessary shared file or new references; proposals and rationale are explicit, and the counterpart need not be installed or invoked.
assertions: Each affected skill has its own documentation placement recommendation, not one generic shared file.
Short optional connections default to SKILL.md only and explain why a reference is unnecessary.
Essential independent inputs, workflow, outputs, boundaries and feedback remain in each SKILL.md.
No automatic cross-skill invocation, implementation change or formal contract is proposed as completed.
The result retains side-by-side considerations and clear evidence/uncertainty distinctions.

evals.prompt: Audit the supplied brief-planning and evidence-refinement skills and recommend documentation organization for a PROPOSED optional integration that would include eight context-field mappings, three conditional handoff scenarios, several examples, and reconciliation guidance. The extra details are proposals from the user, not present in the attached SKILL.md files. Provide per-skill placement recommendations only; do not create files or specify formal schemas.
evals.expected_output: For each affected skill, keep core standalone/optional-handoff instructions in its SKILL.md, and conditionally recommend optional, locally owned references with directional names only where longer details warrant it (e.g. brief-planning/references/brief-to-refinement-handoff.md and evidence-refinement/references/refinement-to-brief-handoff.md). Distinguish source-evidenced behavior from user-proposed details; no mandatory shared file, formal contract or automatic invocation.
assertions: Per-skill decision explicitly explains SKILL.md essentials versus optional reference for substantial details.
Proposed filenames identify direction and belong inside their respective owning skill packages.
No required shared file or cross-skill import is introduced.
Documentation and file paths are PROPOSED rather than represented as existing files.
Formal field schemas and executable integration behavior are deferred.

evals.prompt: Audit the synthetic brief-planning and evidence-refinement skills. They have optional context sharing and an owner-reviewed return path. The user wants an integrated option, but provides no evidence of repeated routing/context-loss problems. Should the audit recommend a coordinator?
evals.expected_output: The audit compares simple optional SKILL.md handoffs and copyable next-action prompts with adding a coordinator, recommends NOT NEEDED or DEFER absent a real coordination burden, and does not default to creating a coordinator. Independent use remains intact.
assertions: A mere optional handoff is not treated as proof a coordinator is required.
Reasons for NOT NEEDED or DEFER cite actual supplied evidence and uncertainty.
Each skill remains independently invocable.
No coordinator file, dispatch code, formal contract, or automatic execution is created or claimed.

evals.prompt: Audit the attached brief-planning and evidence-refinement skills for a combined workflow. The user wants ONE optional entry point that accepts either a feature idea or existing brief, helps select the starting stage, carries source/revision IDs and unanswered questions between two stages, and routes only human-accepted findings back for brief revision. Assume repeated manual copy/paste has been reported by the user, but no host execution trace has been supplied. Recommend an appropriately scoped approach, without implementing it.
evals.expected_output: The audit conditionally recommends a separate optional coordinator skill with routing followed by a short sequential workflow, names owned coordination responsibilities versus independent component responsibilities, compares copyable manual prompts, preserves human approvals, and labels runtime dispatch and the reported copy/paste problem as unverified where applicable.
assertions: Optional coordinator is separately invoked and never required for either skill's standalone entrypoint.
It owns starting-point choice, sequence, context continuity, feedback/approval path, and completion summary—not product/refinement decisions.
Human owner reviews proposed changes; no automatic rewriting or authorization is inferred.
Manual invocation with copyable prompts is compared as an alternative.
Host support, automatic dispatch, actual workflow execution and traces are NOT VERIFIED.
No coordinator SKILL.md or formal dispatch contract is created.

evals.prompt: Audit requirements-review and sprint-readiness; the second expects a required clarity note, and some source files cannot be examined. The user suggests adding a coordinator to fix the missing data. Determine what to recommend.
evals.expected_output: Audit preserves the currently documented required input and flags the missing handoff/ownership question. It defers coordinator selection until requirements and runtime capabilities are established, rather than treating orchestration as a substitute for an absent required input or human review.
assertions: The required clarity note is not silently made optional.
A coordinator is not offered as a fix for missing source data alone.
Lack of evidence supports DEFER / UNVERIFIED or a justified NOT NEEDED, not confident implementation.
Any future coordination is explicitly human-reviewed and separate from original skills.
No runtime execution, source edits, or detailed contracts.

evals.prompt: Audit two synthetic skills with a possible future optional handoff. This is Stage 2 Investigation; the user wants the person reading each skill to understand the integration plan, but explicitly says the skills are NOT yet integrated. An optional direction-specific handoff reference might be helpful later; no such file exists today. Show per-skill proposed documentation and the Stage 3 follow-up without editing targets.
evals.expected_output: The assessment proposes a brief future Optional Handoffs note for each affected SKILL.md, preserves standalone invocation, marks future cross-skill connection PLANNED / PROPOSED — NOT IMPLEMENTED and NOT VERIFIED, names possible directional references only if useful and labels nonexistent files PLANNED — NOT CREATED, and lists unresolved Stage 3 design/contract questions without writing a contract or claiming integration.
assertions: Each affected skill has a separate proposed Optional Handoffs note and retains its own independent inputs, workflow, and outputs.
The intended handoff is clearly a plan, not an existing executed or contracted integration.
Missing optional handoff reference files are not falsely cited as existing or linked as if materialized.
A simple handoff can remain SKILL.md only instead of mandating another file.
Open contract, approval, and feedback decisions are deferred to Stage 3.
No coordinator is built, no source file edited, and no automatic cross-skill invocation is claimed.

evals.prompt: Audit the attached requirements-review and sprint-readiness synthetic skills for a junior developer who is learning engineering investigations. Explain the boundaries finding in plain English while preserving the side-by-side six-consideration layout and source evidence. Do not design contracts.
evals.expected_output: Senior-level, evidence-based assessment explained for a junior developer: compact side-by-side comparison, short vertical explanation of what the authority issue is, why it matters, how documented versus inferred differs, and a bounded human-review recommendation. Does not inflate every finding into a teaching lesson.
assertions: Preserves the original six considerations, four investigation steps and seven report sections.
Defines the relevant meaning of a boundary or duplicated decision authority in plain English when first needed.
Describes a concrete workflow consequence and minimum justified recommendation based on actual inspected source.
Shows direct evidence and does not confuse DOCUMENTED, INFERRED, and OBSERVED runtime results.
Keeps side-by-side cells concise and expands only material findings in vertical notes.
No extra mandatory five-heading lesson, contract design, auto-approval, or source edits.

evals.prompt: Audit brief-planning and evidence-refinement. Explain one well-supported responsibility to KEEP while comparing all six considerations side by side, using per-skill Finding, Evidence, Assessment, Why, Recommendation notes.
evals.expected_output: Evidence-backed KEEP for a sound standalone responsibility with 'keep as-is' and clear reason; meaningful five-field notes below a compact side-by-side comparison, without forced changes.
assertions: Uses a valid KEEP recommendation for a supported responsibility.
Provides five fields only for meaningful findings.
Source evidence status and assessment label are distinct.
No invented defect, approval, contract, source edit or automatic invocation.

evals.prompt: Audit requirements-review and sprint-readiness; both claim final requirements clarity. Show practical reasoning and a clear recommended revision or clarification as the reader encounters the finding; Step 4 should not duplicate all notes.
evals.expected_output: The documented competing ownership receives a grounded CLARIFY or REVISE assessment and practical Why; Step 4 consolidates an actionable human-reviewed suggestion once with independent priority.
assertions: Evidence from both skills supports the conflict.
Assessment and Why explain an actual consequence.
Prioritization is distinct from assessment.
Step 4 consolidates rather than repeats five-field explanation.
Retains six considerations and Stage 2 boundary.

evals.prompt: Audit requirements-review and ticket-drafting; ticket-drafting needs acceptance criteria but no confirmed producer is shown. Explain what can be recommended based on incomplete evidence without inventing a missing implementation.
evals.expected_output: A meaningful VERIFY assessment identifies source/owner evidence needed before suggesting ADD or REVISE; current expected inputs are DOCUMENTED but cross-skill guarantees remain unverified.
assertions: Insufficient evidence leads to VERIFY rather than assuming a runtime failure.
The note gives a specific verification question/action.
Evidence status is separate from assessment and priority.
No extra mandatory columns, contracts, coordinator, edits or approvals.

evals.prompt: Use skill-responsibility-overlap-audit on the attached synthetic discovery-brief skill. Its SKILL.md permits starting provisionally but also says 'If you haven't done discovery yet, run discovery first.' Review this meaningful Inputs/Boundaries wording concern with the existing five finding fields and the optional Current wording, Concern, Recommended wording expansion. Keep it read-only.
evals.expected_output: The exact 'run discovery first' passage is cited; the conflict with provisional drafting is explained in plain English as DOCUMENTED instructions with INFERRED risk of an unnecessary mandatory prerequisite. Assessment CLARIFY is justified and a proposed replacement permits provisional drafting with explicit assumptions and evidence gaps, leaving human approval intact. No extra audit consideration or execution.
assertions: Includes the exact short Current wording from the fixture with source/section citation.
Concern describes a plausible misinterpretation without claiming the skill actually executed discovery.
Recommended wording is PROPOSED and keeps provisional draft and discovery-as-optional-context behavior supported by the fixture.
Uses the core Finding, Evidence, Assessment, Why and Recommendation fields without adding a seventh consideration.
No automatic execution, file edits, approval inference or formal contract.

evals.prompt: Audit the attached approval-evidence synthetic skill. Assess the phrase 'CONFIRMED REQUIREMENT: from a ticket, approved specification, or stakeholder decision.' Propose a precise clarity revision if justified, without claiming ticket content is automatically approved.
evals.expected_output: A sourced wording concern separates stated requirement provenance from actual human approval. Assessment CLARIFY or REVISE and a proposed replacement require independent owner authorization and make explicit that a ticket can contain draft/unapproved scope. Any predicted misuse remains INFERRED.
assertions: Quotes the actual current phrase; identifies its location.
Distinguishes source provenance from authorization and explains why that matters.
Recommended wording preserves read-only behavior and no automatic approval.
No unsupported behavioral observation, source edit, new contract or invented owner approval.

evals.prompt: Audit the attached clear-evidence synthetic skill. Its optional discovery and approval wording is already clear. Should the audit generate Current wording, Concern, Recommended wording sections just to fill a template?
evals.expected_output: KEEP the clear standalone/optional input and authorization guidance with a concise reason. Do not force wording concern or recommended wording when no material ambiguity is evidenced.
assertions: KEEP is supported by clear source wording and avoids unnecessary changes.
Does not generate a contrived Current wording/Concern/Recommended wording block.
Still gives appropriate evidence and human-review boundaries.
Does not invent runtime enforcement from written restrictions or modify files.

evals.prompt: Compare requirements-review and sprint-readiness using Skill Responsibility & Overlap Audit. Keep the side-by-side comparison.

Material F-xx identifiers and Finding/Evidence/Assessment/Why/Recommendation are present inline in the correct skill cell; no HTML markup or literal line-break tags.
No detached Finding A/B/C section or duplicated five-field findings after the comparison.
Cross-skill effects are referenced by F-xx and Cx without invented evidence.
Source evidence and proposed Stage 2 changes remain clearly distinct from runtime observations.

evals.prompt: Audit discovery-brief and approval-evidence. Show Current wording, Concern and Recommended wording — PROPOSED within the existing C-row skill cell if concise, or in an adjacent F-xx wording row when a quote is longer. Restore readable Markdown tables, without HTML.

No literal HTML tags or extra columns, and no separate findings section.
Source text is DOCUMENTED, behavioral risk INFERRED unless runtime evidence exists, and replacement PROPOSED.
Recommended wording preserves existing approval and safety requirements.
Step 4 references original F-xx without duplicating long exact wording.

evals.prompt: Compare four synthetic skills: requirements-review, sprint-readiness, ticket-drafting, and estimation-advisor. Use small grouped tables when needed, but retain row-level F-xx notes in cells and stable C1–C6 IDs. Demonstrate how a finding connected to multiple considerations is cross-referenced without duplicating the full finding.
evals.expected_output: Grouped, readable Markdown tables cover four skills with concise inline F-xx finding summaries in their primary C1–C6 skill cells. Related considerations use F-xx references. Material F-xx and Cx IDs are inside or immediately adjacent to their primary consideration row, not detached below.
No HTML tags or forced multi-line content inside Markdown table cells.
Related consideration cross-references do not duplicate full findings.
Grouped two- or three-skill tables remain readable and preserve human-review and read-only boundaries.

evals.prompt: Run skill-responsibility-overlap-audit on the supplied requirements-review and sprint-readiness synthetic skills in a plain-text terminal that displays raw HTML tags literally. Render the six-consideration side-by-side Markdown report with F-xx assessment, reason and recommendation fields. Prior formatting broke because field lines were separated by HTML markup. Only three table columns: Consideration, Skill A, Skill B; normal terminal wrapping is allowed.
Meaningful F-xx finding includes an assessment, evidence, why and recommendation tied to its Cx row.
No fabricated runtime claim, contract design, source edit or auto-approval.
Step 4 references F-xx without reprinting entire finding.

evals.prompt: Audit the synthetic discovery-brief SKILL.md in a narrow terminal. An exact discovery-prerequisite quote and proposed revision are long. Keep the C1 Inputs finding visible in the same consideration group while preventing a giant broken HTML-filled cell. Show what to do when wording is lengthy.

Full exact wording and proposed replacement appear immediately after the C1 row in a single additional F-xx wording/detail row or adjacent block, without extra columns or raw HTML. assertions: Original Inputs consideration is clear and remains linked to F-xx.
Exact Current wording / Concern / Recommended wording are adjacent to the finding and not a detached section.
